acceptedAnswer.text: Modern root canal treatment is performed under local anaesthesia, which means the area is fully numbed before the procedure begins. Most patients find the treatment itself no more uncomfortable than having a filling. The discomfort people often associate with root canals is usually caused by the underlying infection rather than the treatment. Following the procedure, some mild tenderness is normal for a few days and can typically be managed with over-the-counter pain relief as advised by your dentist.

mainEntity.name: Can an infected tooth heal on its own without treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, once the dental pulp becomes infected, it cannot heal without professional intervention. The enclosed nature of the root canal system limits the body's ability to fight the infection effectively. While symptoms may sometimes diminish temporarily — particularly if the nerve dies — the underlying bacterial infection typically continues. Regular dental assessments help monitor at-risk teeth and identify infections that may not be causing obvious symptoms.

mainEntity.name: How long can you leave a tooth that needs a root canal?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no fixed timeframe, as each situation is different. Some infections progress slowly over months or years, while others can develop more rapidly. Delaying treatment generally allows the infection more time to spread, which may make eventual treatment more complex or reduce the likelihood of saving the tooth. If your dentist has recommended root canal treatment, it is advisable to discuss the timing and any concerns you may have so that an appropriate plan can be made.

mainEntity.name: What are the alternatives to root canal treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main alternative to root canal treatment is extraction — removing the tooth entirely. While this eliminates the source of infection, it also means losing the natural tooth, which may then need to be replaced with an implant, bridge, or denture to restore function and appearance. In some very early cases, other approaches may be considered, but these depend on the specific clinical findings. Your dentist will explain all suitable options during your consultation.

mainEntity.name: Can antibiotics cure a tooth infection without a root canal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Antibiotics may be prescribed to help manage the spread of a dental infection, particularly if there is significant swelling or systemic symptoms. However, antibiotics alone do not typically eliminate the source of infection within the tooth. The bacteria reside inside the root canal system, which has a limited blood supply, making it difficult for antibiotics to reach the area effectively. Antibiotics are generally used as a supportive measure alongside dental treatment rather than as a standalone solution.

mainEntity.name: How much does root canal treatment cost privately in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of root canal treatment varies depending on several factors, including the tooth involved, the complexity of the root canal system, and the type of restoration required afterwards. Front teeth typically have simpler root systems and may cost less than molars, which have multiple roots. During your consultation, your dentist will provide a clear treatment plan and cost breakdown so that you can make an informed decision. Many practices also offer payment plans to help manage costs.
